title: Signature Logical-to-Physical Mapping — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Archives outlive their storage: files migrate from disk to disk while their logical identity stays fixed, so a mapping table translates the stable logical name to wherever the bytes live today. The resolver consults this table on every access, which means migrations update one table instead of every reference. Entries carry a version stamp so concurrent migrations cannot silently overwrite each other. This indirection is the same idea as virtual memory — programs use stable addresses while hardware moves pages underneath. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — Signature original authored for Justin Addam Higgins.

title: Signature Indirection Chains — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Sometimes resolution takes several hops: a logical name points to an alias, the alias points to a replica set, the replica set points to the live node. The resolver follows these chains hop by hop with a loop guard, because a misconfigured alias can point back at itself. Each hop is logged, so a slow resolution can be diagnosed as a chain that grew too long. Chains give administrators freedom to reorganize storage without ever breaking the names users saved. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Migration Redirects — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. When a file moves permanently, the old location keeps a redirect to the new one for a grace period, exactly like HTTP redirects on the web. Resolvers follow the redirect automatically and can optionally update the caller's stored reference to skip the hop next time. Redirect chains are collapsed periodically so no resolution pays for ancient history. This is how archives reorganize petabytes without breaking a single saved link. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Mirror Selection — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. A logical file often exists in several places at once — the primary archive, a regional mirror, a tape backup staged to disk. The resolver picks among mirrors using freshness, measured bandwidth, and the requester's location, preferring the copy that will deliver fastest without being stale. If the chosen mirror fails mid-transfer, resolution falls through to the next candidate transparently. Mirror selection turns redundancy from a backup strategy into a performance strategy. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature TTL-Cached Resolution — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Resolving the same logical name thousands of times per second would swamp the mapping service, so resolutions are cached with a time-to-live. A short TTL — seconds to minutes — absorbs the hot-path load while still picking up migrations quickly. Cache entries are versioned against the mapping table, so a migration can proactively invalidate exactly the affected names. TTL caching is the standard compromise between always-fresh and always-fast in naming systems from DNS to service meshes. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
